# Issue tracker: GitHub Issues (via the gh CLI)

Specs and tickets for this repo live as GitHub Issues in **burythehammer/claude-code-plugins**. The
**`gh` CLI** is the only route — every operation below is a `gh` command, and
every one takes `-R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins` explicitly. The repository is pinned in
config; never re-resolve it from the working directory, which may be a worktree,
a fork, or somewhere else entirely.

An issue id looks like `#42`. A bare `42` means the same thing. Pull requests
share the number space but are **not** a triage surface here: filter them out by
using `gh issue` rather than `gh pr`, which does that for you.

## Preflight

Before the first operation in a session:

    gh auth status
    gh repo view burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json viewerPermission,nameWithOwner,hasIssuesEnabled

Stop and report if `gh` is missing or unauthenticated, if `viewerPermission` is
below `WRITE`, or if `hasIssuesEnabled` is `false`. GitHub is the backend, not
an optional mirror; there is no local fallback. This preflight writes nothing
and leaves nothing behind. It is not the capability probe, which ran once at
config time.

## Two axes: status vs triage labels

Issues here carry two independent axes. Do not conflate them:

- **Status** belongs to the delivery lifecycle and is driven by specflow's
  lifecycle skills (`/tfuk-specflow:start`, `pick`, `close`). Triage must not
  change status, with one exception: closing a `wontfix` (see Close below).
- **Triage states** live in **bare labels** — see `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`
  for the state → label mapping.
- **Category** (`bug`, `enhancement`, `chore`) is a third axis, also bare
  labels, and deliberately not a projection of `spec_type`: an issue may carry a
  category, a type and a triage state at once. Same doc.

## Status

GitHub has no status field, so status is carried by a `status:` label while the
issue is open, and by the issue being **closed** once it is done:

| Canonical status | How it is stored                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `ready`          | open, label `status:ready`            |
| `in-progress`    | open, label `status:in-progress`      |
| `in-review`      | open, label `status:in-review`        |
| `done`           | **closed** (no `status:` label)       |

**Raw status** is the `status:` label while open, and `closed` once closed. Mind
the casing: `--json state` returns `OPEN` / `CLOSED`, so lower-case it before
comparing it against a canonical value. Read both axes in one call:

    gh issue view 42 -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json state,stateReason,labels

An issue carries **at most one** `status:` label. Moving status means adding the
incoming label and removing the outgoing one in the same call; there are no
intermediate hops to walk, because there is no workflow engine:

    gh issue edit 42 -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-label status:in-progress --remove-label status:ready

Reaching `done` means closing, and closing means dropping the `status:` label so
a reopened issue does not claim a stale one:

    gh issue close 42 -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --reason completed --comment "<progress comment>"
    gh issue edit 42 -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --remove-label status:in-review

## Issue types

`spec_type` is stored in **`label` mode**, decided when this repo
was configured:

- **`native` mode** — set `type` in the create's request, as under Create an
  issue. Native issue types are defined per organisation, so this mode exists
  only where the owning organisation has configured them.
- **`label` mode** — apply a `type:<spec_type>` label instead. This is always
  the answer for a user-owned repository, which cannot have native types at all.

`spec_type` → type name, from config:

- bug → bug
- chore → chore
- feature → feature
- other → other
- refactor → refactor
- spike → spike

**Never send a `type` speculatively, and never try it and fall back.** When the
named type does not exist, the create can fail after it has made the issue,
leaving an untyped issue behind; a retry would then create a second one.
Use the mode above and nothing else.

## Priority

Priority is a label, `priority:1` (highest) through `priority:5`. The suffix is
the canonical integer itself, so there is no name-to-number table to keep in
sync. At most one per issue, added and removed like any other label. Setting it
adds the incoming label and, where the issue carries one, removes the outgoing
one in the same call:

    gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-label priority:2 --remove-label priority:3

## Record triage findings

What triage verified is written on the spec, as a dated section at the end of
its body, so it outlives the session. There is no per-section edit, so it is the
whole-body edit in Conventions below:

1. `gh issue view <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json body`, immediately before writing.
2. Append `## Update from triage (<ISO date>)` and the findings beneath it, or,
   where today's section is already there, add the findings to its end. Then `gh
   issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md` with
   the whole body.

The heading is plain text, with no backticks or emphasis in it. A re-triage on
the same day extends that day's section, and one on a later day adds a new
section. An earlier day's section is never edited. No findings means no section.

## Close a duplicate

A duplicate closes as a `wontfix` whose comment names the original, once what
only the duplicate holds is carried into the original:

1. Record triage findings (above) on the original. The section opens `Carried
   from #<duplicate>:` and then lists the duplicate's criteria the original
   lacks and its findings, as a plain list rather than task items. Nothing
   unique to carry: skip this step.
2. `gh issue comment <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file
   .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`, the body opening `Duplicate of #<original>.`
   and saying in a sentence what the original already covers. GitHub reads that
   opening line and marks the issue a duplicate in its timeline.
3. `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-label wontfix --remove-label
   <the outgoing triage label>`.
4. Close the duplicate's open tickets (below), as a duplicate of the
   original.
5. `gh issue close <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --reason "not planned"`, then remove
   the `status:` label, as in Close below.

## Close a spec's open tickets

When a spec closes, its open tickets close with it, and a rewrite closes the old
set's (`Rewrite a spec in place` below). Read the set from the spec's sub-issues
(`gh issue view <spec> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json subIssues`), whose nodes carry
each ticket's `state`. For each open one:

1. `gh issue comment <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file
   .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`, the body one line: `Closed with its spec
   #<spec>, closed as <already implemented / a duplicate of #<original> / its
   reason>.`
2. `gh issue close <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --reason completed`. Tickets carry no
   `status:` label, so there is none to remove.

A ticket already closed is left as it is. A ticket takes no `wontfix` label —
the triage state is the spec's.

## Rewrite a spec in place

A spec that already exists is redrafted in its own issue, never a new one:

1. `gh issue view <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json title,body`, then post that body as
   a comment, `gh issue comment <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file
   .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`, opening `The description before this
   rewrite:`.
2. Replace the body with the new draft. Write the title to
   `.tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>-title.txt` with the Write tool, holding the new
   title where the draft retitles it and the current one where it does not, then
   send both from files, so neither reaches a command line:

   ```bash
   jq -n --rawfile title .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>-title.txt --rawfile body .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md \
     '{title: ($title | rtrimstr("\n")), body: $body}' > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-issue.json
   gh api --method PATCH repos/burythehammer/claude-code-plugins/issues/<n> --input .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-issue.json
   ```

   Labels and assignees stay as they are. Carry the body's `## Related specs`
   section into the draft unchanged, since the body is replaced whole and the
   section is where the relations live.
3. Once the new set is published (The ticket set below), close the old set's
   open tickets per `Close a spec's open tickets` above: only those read before
   the new set was cut, never a new one. Each comment reads `Closed by the
   rewrite of #<spec>: its new ticket set replaces this one.`

## Rank

Issues carry no order of their own beyond their priority label, so there is
nothing to rank within a priority. The rank pass still raises blockers: save the
listing per § Listing specs to pick, then run `specflow-preflight.py rank-plan
--repo . --caller groom <listing>`. Blocker edges are the native dependencies
the listing carries, on specs and on tickets. Its `raises` and `cycles` are read
as on Jira. The pass then ends with `Ranking isn't available on github-issues:
specs there are ordered by priority alone.`

## Epics

Epics aren't available on github-issues yet: a spec here has no epic to belong
to. The groom `epic` pass ends with `Epics aren't available on github-issues
yet.` before any read or write.

## Conventions

- **Create an issue**: write the title to `.tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>-title.txt`
  with the Write tool, as the body is written, then build the request from both
  files and send it. Neither the title nor the body reaches a command line:

  ```bash
  jq -n --rawfile title .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>-title.txt --rawfile body .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md \
    --argjson labels '["<label>", …]' \
    '{title: ($title | rtrimstr("\n")), body: $body, labels: $labels}' > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-issue.json
  gh api --method POST repos/burythehammer/claude-code-plugins/issues --input .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-issue.json > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-reply.json
  jq '{number, id}' .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-reply.json
  ```

  A non-zero exit means no issue exists: report `gh`'s message, not the reply.
  `number` is `<n>` for the calls below, and `id` is the new issue's database
  id, which the links need. Then, for each as it applies:

  - **Assignee**: `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-assignee "@me"`.
  - **Parent**: `jq '{sub_issue_id: .id}' .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-reply.json >
    .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-sub-issue.json`, then `gh api --method POST
    repos/burythehammer/claude-code-plugins/issues/<spec-number>/sub_issues --input
    .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-sub-issue.json`.
  - **Each blocker `<m>`**: `gh api repos/burythehammer/claude-code-plugins/issues/<m> --jq
    '{issue_id: .id}' > .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-blocked-by.json`, then `gh api
    --method POST repos/burythehammer/claude-code-plugins/issues/<n>/dependencies/blocked_by --input
    .tfuk-specflow/tmp/github-blocked-by.json`. Publish blockers first, so each
    `<m>` is a real number.
  - **Native type**, in `native` mode only: add `--arg type '<type name>'` to the
    `jq` call and `type: $type` to its object, with the name from the map above.

  Bodies are markdown, passed by file so newlines and backticks survive the
  shell. Write each body file with the Write tool into `.tfuk-specflow/tmp/` of
  the working copy you are in, so `gh` reads it from inside the working
  directory, which a user's read boundary always allows. The directory is
  gitignored, and a file there stays for the next write to overwrite.
- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json
  number,title,body,state,stateReason,labels,assignees,issueType,parent,subIssues,subIssuesSummary,blockedBy,blocking`
  — one call for every field the lifecycle skills need. Add `--comments` to read
  the discussion.
- **List / query**: `gh issue list -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins [--label …] [--state
  open|closed|all] [--assignee …] [--search <q>] [--limit N] --json …`. Worked
  queries:
  - Untriaged: `gh issue list -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --search '-label:needs-triage
    -label:needs-info -label:needs-clarify -label:ready-for-agent
    -label:ready-for-human -label:wontfix' --json number,title`
  - In a triage state: `gh issue list -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --label needs-triage`
    (etc.)
  - Ready for agents: `gh issue list -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --label ready-for-agent
    --label status:ready` — repeated `--label` flags are ANDed.
- **Own a spec**: `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-assignee "@me"` — the
  same call that claims a ticket, applied to the spec when work starts on it.
  Owned = has assignees, so an existing owner is knowable and is never
  overwritten.
- **Comment**: `gh issue comment <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file
  .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`.
- **Labels**: `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-label <name>
  --remove-label <name>`. Always remove the outgoing triage label when applying
  the incoming one — an issue carries at most one state label. Labels must
  already exist (see `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`).
- **Edit the body**: `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file
  .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`. There is no per-section edit, so a body change
  is always read the whole body, change the part you mean, write the whole body
  back. Read it with `--json body` immediately before writing, so a concurrent
  edit is not silently discarded.
- **Close**: close the spec's open tickets (`Close a spec's open tickets`
  above), then `gh issue close <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --reason completed`, then
  remove the `status:` label. For a `wontfix`: apply the label, post the
  explanation comment, close the open tickets, then close with `--reason "not
  planned"` — the label records *why*, and `--json stateReason` reads back
  `NOT_PLANNED` so the distinction survives without the label. The spec's own
  close is always the last write.
- **Reopen**: `gh issue reopen <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins`, then add the `status:`
  label the issue should carry.

## Acceptance-criteria mechanics

Acceptance criteria are an `## Acceptance criteria` heading whose body is a task
list — one `- [ ]` line per criterion, implicitly numbered `AC-1`, `AC-2`, … by
order. specflow's lifecycle skills parse this structure — an issue without it is
invisible to downstream automation.

GitHub gives a task-list item no handle of its own, so ticking one is
read-modify-write on the whole body:

1. `gh issue view <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json body` and write the body to a file
   in `.tfuk-specflow/tmp/`.
2. Find the criterion's line by an **exact single-line match** on its text. If
   it does not appear exactly once, **refuse to write** and report the count —
   zero means the criterion text has drifted from the issue, and two or more
   means a blind edit would tick the wrong one.
3. Flip that line's `[ ]` to `[x]`, changing nothing else. Never renumber or
   reorder.
4. `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`,
   then read the body back and verify **exactly one line** differs from the body
   you started from.

## Publish a spec

The create under Create an issue, open, with the `status:ready` label, the
`ready-for-agent` triage label, the `spec_type` carried per the mode above, and
a `priority:<n>` label if priority is known. Two hard requirements on the body,
whatever template the skill brought with it:

1. An `## Acceptance criteria` task list (mechanics above). If the source
   template has no acceptance-criteria section (e.g. user stories and testing
   decisions instead), **derive checkable criteria from those sections and add
   it** — keep the template's own sections too.
2. Section order and names beyond that are free; prefer: Problem statement,
   Scope (in/out), Acceptance criteria, Technical notes.

## Telling a spec from a ticket

Issue numbers are the same shape either way, so read the issue's parent:

    gh issue view <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json parent

A null `parent` is a spec. A non-null one is a ticket — or a wayfinder map's
child, which its own `wayfinder:<type>` label distinguishes.

## The ticket set

Every published spec carries a set of tracer-bullet tickets — `to-tickets` cuts
them, blockers first. The structure is native, so nothing about the set lives in
prose:

- **Parent reference**: the ticket is a **sub-issue** of the spec. Link it at
  creation with the parent call under Create an issue, or `gh issue edit <n>
  --parent <spec-number>` afterwards. Read it back with `--json parent`. The
  spec body never lists its tickets: keeping a hand-written list beside a native
  one is how the two drift apart.
- **Canonical set record**: the spec's own sub-issue list.

      gh issue view <spec> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json subIssues,subIssuesSummary

  `subIssues.nodes` gives the set, in order, each with `number`, `title` and
  `state`; `subIssuesSummary` gives `{completed, total, percentCompleted}`,
  which is set progress without a second call. List a spec's set this way —
  never by text search.
- **Blocking edges**: native dependencies. The blocker calls under Create an
  issue link them at creation, `gh issue edit <n> --add-blocked-by <m>` /
  `--remove-blocked-by <m>` afterwards. Publish blockers first so the flags
  can name real numbers. A ticket is **unblocked** when every entry in its
  `blockedBy` is closed:

      gh issue view <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json blockedBy

  Each node carries `number`, `state` and `title`, so one call answers both
  *what blocks this* and *is it done*. The edge is reciprocal — the blocker
  reports the same relationship under `blocking`. Dependencies work on
  user-owned repositories as well as organisation ones.
- **Ticket lifecycle is two-state**: open or closed. Tickets do not carry
  `status:` labels — the spec's status is the spec's, and a ticket's own
  progress is its open/closed state plus its ticked criteria.
- **Claim**: `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-assignee "@me"`. Unclaimed
  = no assignees. Compare an existing assignee against `gh api user --jq .login`
  to tell our own claim from someone else's.
- **Frontier**: open, unblocked, unclaimed, first in set order. Read the set
  from the spec's own `subIssues` rather than a repo-wide issue list. Coming the
  other way — from a candidate issue rather than from its spec — resolve `gh
  issue view <n> --json parent` and skip anything whose parent carries
  `wayfinder:map`: a map's children are structurally identical to a spec's
  tickets, and that label is the only thing telling them apart.
- **Close a ticket**: post the progress comment, then close with `--reason
  completed`.

## Spec blockers

One spec waits on another through the same native dependency a ticket uses,
drawn between the two specs themselves. It needs no sub-issues on either side,
so a spec still in the clarify queue can be ordered.

- **Write one**: `gh issue edit <waiting spec> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --add-blocked-by
  <blocking spec>`. `--remove-blocked-by` removes it, as for a ticket.
- **Read one**: `gh issue view <spec> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json blockedBy` lists
  the spec's blockers. Its nodes carry no parent, so read each entry's own
  `--json parent`, as in § Telling a spec from a ticket: a null `parent` is a
  spec blocker, cleared once that issue is closed.
- **Never in prose.** An ordering written into a body ("pick after #12") is read
  by nothing. Add the dependency and remove the prose.
- **One ticket's wait stays a ticket edge.** Where only one ticket of the
  waiting spec depends on the other spec, add the dependency to that ticket,
  naming the ticket it waits on. The ticket set's rules apply to it as they do
  to any edge, across specs as within one.

## Related specs

Two specs are related when neither's scope can be decided without reading the
other: they are read together, and neither waits on the other. The relation is a
`## Related specs` section in the body of both issues, each naming the other as
`#<n>`, one per line:

    ## Related specs

    - #12

- **Write one**: edit both issues' bodies so each carries the section naming the
  other, `gh issue edit <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file
  .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`, with the rest of the body left as it stands.
- **Read them**: `gh issue view <spec> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json body`, and the
  `#<n>` entries under `## Related specs`. Each is related, and the relation is
  symmetric, so a spec naming another counts even where the other does not name
  it back.
- **Remove one**: take the entry out of both bodies. A section left with no
  entries is removed with its heading.
- **A duplicate close draws none.** A duplicate is closed, not related (`Close a
  duplicate` above), so a duplicate's comment stays the one record of it.
- **Relations stay after a close.** A closed related spec keeps its section, so
  clarify can still see that it may have met criteria the open spec needs.

## Record a spec's PR

The PR a spec raised is recorded on the spec, as a comment whose first line is
`PR raised: <url> into <base>.`, so it outlives the branch:

- **Write it**: `gh issue comment <spec> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --body-file
  .tfuk-specflow/tmp/<name>.md`, the body that one line.
- **Read it**: `gh issue view <spec> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json comments`, filtered
  to bodies opening `PR raised:`. The newest by `createdAt` is the spec's PR
  and its base. None: the spec has no recorded PR.
- **Skip a repeat**: write none where the newest already names the same PR and
  base. A changed base, or another PR, gets a new comment. Older ones stay.

A recorded link counts only where all of it matches
`^https://[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?(/[A-Za-z0-9._~%-]+)*/pulls?/[0-9]+$`, which
allows no whitespace, quotes, `;`, backticks or `$`. Anything else is no
record, as the link reaches a command.

## Listing specs to pick

What `/pick` hands `specflow-preflight.py classify-specs` when no spec is
active. Specs and tickets come in one listing, saved as gh prints it:

    gh issue list -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --state open --limit 500 \
      --json number,title,state,labels,assignees,parent,blockedBy,subIssuesSummary \
      > <scratch file>

Pass that file's path as the listing, and `gh api user --jq .login` as `--me`. A
listing of exactly 500 issues may have been cut short: raise `--limit` and list
again.

For `/groom` only, the comments of the open `needs-info` specs, so the triage
queue can hold back those still waiting on their reporter:

    gh issue list -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --label needs-info --state open --json number,comments --limit 500 \
      > <scratch file>

A reply of exactly 500 issues may have been cut short: raise `--limit` and read
again. Pass that file's path as `--needs-info-file`. With no open `needs-info`
spec, the reply is `[]`: omit the flag.

## Branch

Create a ticket's branch through GitHub, so the issue's Development section
links the work:

    gh issue develop <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --name <branch-name> --base <trunk> --checkout

`--name` is what keeps the repo's own naming convention: GitHub's default name
is derived from the issue title, and passing `--name` overrides it. The prefix
and slug rules are **not** here — they live in `docs/agents/conventions.md`,
which is the only source for what `<branch-name>` should be. Both it and
`--base`, the trunk, arrive here already resolved.

Already on the intended branch: nothing to do. The branch exists already,
locally or on the remote: `git switch` to it (a second `gh issue develop` would
create a suffixed duplicate). Only create when it does not exist. `gh issue
develop <n> --list` shows what is already linked.

`gh issue develop` needs the network and it needs `gh` authenticated. When it
fails, the link is the part that is lost, not the work: fall back to plain git —
`git switch -c <branch-name> --no-track origin/<trunk>`, or the local trunk if
there is no remote — and say the branch is unlinked, so the link can be made
later with `gh issue develop <n> --name <branch-name>`.

## Who writes what

During intake, `/tfuk-specflow:start` publishes the spec and the ticket set that
`to-spec` and `to-tickets` shape — the Pocock Suite thinks, specflow writes.
`implement-spec` builds, merges and commits only. specflow's `pick` claims each
ticket as its implementer starts and, as the ticket's merge lands, records:
ticks the spec's acceptance criteria the ticket covered, posts the progress
comment, closes the ticket, and moves the spec's status. Working outside `start`
or `pick` and unsure whether to write? Don't — report instead.

## Conventions for building

How work is written — commit format, branch conventions, test and typecheck
commands, PR rules — lives in `docs/agents/conventions.md`. `implement-spec`,
`tdd`, and `code-review` (its standards axis) read that doc, not this one.

## Fetch the relevant ticket

`gh issue view <n> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json …` with `--comments` — the body **is**
the spec/ticket; read it and the comments before acting.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `wayfinder`. Its labels are used verbatim, colon included:
`wayfinder:map`, `wayfinder:<type>` (types: `research`, `prototype`, `grilling`,
`task`).

- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map` holding Destination / Notes /
  Decisions-so-far / Not-yet-specified. A map carries no `status:` label — it is
  not a spec and has no delivery lifecycle. Owned by whoever charted it, as its
  assignee — who to ask before working the effort. Its child tickets stay
  unassigned, or the frontier filter drops every candidate.
- **Child ticket**: an ordinary issue labelled `wayfinder:<type>`, created as a
  **sub-issue of the map** (the parent call under Create an issue, with the
  map's number), with native blocked-by edges exactly as in the ticket set above.
- **Frontier query** — a map's children and a spec's tickets are structurally
  identical, so the map's label is what separates them. Read the map's own
  sub-issue list and filter:

      gh issue view <map> -R burythehammer/claude-code-plugins --json subIssues

  then, for each open candidate, `gh issue view <n> --json assignees,blockedBy`
  and drop it if it is claimed or if any `blockedBy` entry is still open. Coming
  the other way — from a candidate rather than a map — resolve `--json parent`
  and skip anything whose parent does not carry `wayfinder:map`.
- **Claim**: `--add-assignee "@me"` — before any work.
- **Resolve**: comment with the answer, close with `--reason completed`, then
  append a context pointer to the map's Decisions-so-far by the
  read-modify-write body edit above.
- Research assets stay linked from the child issue, not pasted in.
